episodes.160217: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms that developed over Brevard County and pushed offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Intracoastal Waterway.
episodes.160334: A line of strong thunderstorms moved from southeast and east central Wisconsin across the Lake Michigan shore and nearshore areas during the afternoon, producing sporadic strong wind gusts in excess of 30 knots.
episodes.160382: During the early morning of Tuesday, August 24th, a broken line of storms developed across North Dakota and rapidly moved east-southeast toward west-central Minnesota. There were several surges along the broken line of storms that produced severe wind gusts and damaging winds. A few large hailstones also occurred within this line of storms. As the storms moved eastward, the severity lowered with wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph.
episodes.160400: Numerous evening thunderstorms moved across Seminole County, with one becoming severe over Sanford, and resulting in tree and home damage.
episodes.160709: Afternoon storms produce a strong marine wind gust in Pinellas offshore waters.
episodes.160716: Thunderstorms developed across south central and southwest WI, and moved into east-central and southeast Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours. The initial round of strong storms that dived south along and inland from Lake Michigan produced strong thunderstorm outflow, of 40 to 50 mph out ahead of the main line of storms. Additional storms that developed across southwest WI caused wind damage in portions of Lafayette County.
episodes.160784: As the remnants from former Hurricane Linda pushed through the islands; heavy showers fell over most of the state, with Maui, the Big Island, Molokai, and Oahu being the most affected.  The rain caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.160886: The local sheriff in Dunn County reported two individuals that were working at a construction site in Menomonie, Wisconsin, Tuesday morning, August 24th, were struck by lightning.||A 60-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene. A 20-year-old man was taken to Mayo in Eau Claire with serious injuries.||Dunn County authorities said the crew was working on a pole shed under a partial roof on ladders when the lightning struck.
episodes.161014: A cluster of severe storms developed in northwestern South Dakota during the late afternoon hours and migrated east, crossing north central and northeast South Dakota through the overnight and early morning hours. This was primarily a wind producing complex with gusts in excess of 100 mph at times which caused sporadic damage.
episodes.161079: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northern Illinois during the afternoon and evening of August 24th.
episodes.161080: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon and evening of August 24th.
episodes.161163: A narrow upper level trough was across the region which triggered numerous showers and storms over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.161190: Several rounds of thunderstorms tracked across central and east-central Wisconsin during the morning and early afternoon hours. The strongest storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.161191: Strong thunderstorms produced gusty winds as they tracked over the Lake Michigan nearshore waters during the early afternoon hours.
episodes.161280: Severe storms resulted in numerous reports of wind damage.
episodes.161345: Thunderstorms moved through the southern James River Valley as an upper level short-wave trough and affiliated surface low moved over the region. While most of the severe weather remained over South Dakota, one thunderstorm produced severe wind gusts estimated at 65 mph over the Ellendale area in Dickey County.
episodes.161386: Severe thunderstorms developed across a good portion of eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois on the afternoon of Tuesday August 24th, 2021. A corridor of very strong winds was observed along the Highway 20 corridor from Fairbank IA, to Hazelton IA and to Manchester IA, where numerous reports of damage to trees, homes and power outages were received. Hail up to golf ball size was also observed in Manchester IA.||Storms continued to track south and east, with an outflow boundary producing strong winds into portions of northwest Illinois including the Quad Cities metro. Additional reports of wind damage were received across northwest Illinois, with a 66 MPH wind gust measured at the Savanna, IL AWOS.
episodes.161387: Severe thunderstorms developed across a good portion of eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois on the afternoon of Tuesday August 24th, 2021. A corridor of very strong winds was observed along the Highway 20 corridor from Fairbank IA, to Hazelton IA and to Manchester IA, where numerous reports of damage to trees, homes and power outages were received. Hail up to golf ball size was also observed in Manchester IA.||Storms continued to track south and east, with an outflow boundary producing strong winds into portions of northwest Illinois including the Quad Cities metro. Additional reports of wind damage were received across northwest Illinois, with a 66 MPH wind gust measured at the Savanna, IL AWOS.
episodes.161932: Thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours over northwest North Dakota as an upper level short-wave trough and affiliated surface low moved through the region. One storm became severe, producing half-dollar size hail south of Minot in Ward County.
episodes.162019: A broad area of low pressure developed across coastal waters, helping produce scattered thunderstorms with gusty winds.
episodes.162020: A broad area of low pressure developing across the region helped produced strong to severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina during peak heating hours.
episodes.162072: A hot an humid air mass settled across the area with plenty of ambient instability available. As a complex of storms moved across Minnesota in the morning hours they put out an outflow boundary that moved into northern Iowa in the early afternoon. This provided just enough lift within such an unstable environment to initiate two main clusters of thunderstorms, producing some small hail along with gusty winds that caused tree and minor structural damage in north central Iowa.
episodes.162079: An isolated early morning storm produced severe wind gust across Cherry County.
episodes.162331: Thunderstorms moving through in the evening hours produced sporadic wind damage, mainly north of M-59.
episodes.162333: Thunderstorms moving through Saginaw Bay produced wind gusts around 40 knots.
episodes.162396: A line of storms rolled across western Wisconsin during the morning of August 24th. A lightning strike from these storms struck a gas line and started a fire in Eleva (Trempeauleau County). The storms also produced winds strong enough to blow down trees and power lines near Owen (Clark County). Around 900 customers were without power across northern Clark County following the passage of the storm.
episodes.162397: A line of storms rolled across northeast Iowa during the afternoon of August 24th. These storms produced winds strong enough to cause wind damage from Floyd County east across Chickasaw County into Fayette County. Trees were downed along U.S. Highway 63 near New Hampton (Chickasaw County) and 60 mph wind gusts in Oelwein (Fayette County) snapped and uprooted numerous trees and caused a building to partially collapse. One person was injured in Oelwein when they became trapped under the branches of a fallen tree. The Governor of Iowa issued a proclamation of disaster emergency for Fayette County.
episodes.162399: A line of storms rolled across southwest Wisconsin during the afternoon of August 24th. These storms produced wind gust around 60 mph in Dickeyville (Grant County) and Hazel Green (Grant County). Trees were blown down and tin was ripped off a shed near Cuba City (Grant County).
episodes.162560: Scattered strong storms occurred across the coastal water with multiple reports of a waterspout off the panhandle coast along with gusty winds offshore and along the big bend coast.
episodes.162684: A large outflow boundary from a late night convective complex across northeast South Dakota and west central MN pushed southward, and interacted with a strong low-level jet. With steep mid-level lapse rates present, convective initiation resulted in intense updrafts along the boundary which produced large hail.
episodes.162685: A large outflow boundary from a late night convective complex across northeast South Dakota and west central MN pushed southward, and interacted with a strong low-level jet. With steep mid-level lapse rates present, convective initiation resulted in intense updrafts along the boundary which produced large hail.
episodes.162817: Isolated severe thunderstorms impacted portions of southeastern North Dakota during the early morning hours of Aug 24th.
episodes.162880: An MCS that initiated during the early morning hours of 8/24 along the Minnesota/Wisconsin border quickly trekked east during the day, eventually making it into southern portions of the forecast area by the evening. Strong winds associated with this line of storms resulted in trees and powerlines down across parts of Gladwin county.
episodes.163038: A broken line of thunderstorms moved into southeastern Lake Michigan, producing strong winds.

A storm survey conducted by NWS Melbourne confirms that a severe thunderstorm produced a small area of peak straight-line winds estimated between 55 and 65 mph, mainly within the Pinecrest Subdivision of Sanford. These winds caused several large trees to snap or uproot. Numerous large branches were also downed throughout the area. A few trees and many large branches fell onto roofs and blocked roadways. Damage to a few homes, sheds, garages, and fences occurred. Surrounding this area, a larger zone of winds estimated between 45 and 55 mph impacted portions of north-central Seminole County, near and west of the Orlando-Sanford International Airport. A peak wind gust of 43 mph was recorded by the ASOS (KSFB) at 1825LST. Within this area, mostly minor damage to trees and branches was observed.
